Menu

What visitors mention

Items named in public listings. No prices shown; this is not a verified menu. Photos are illustrative stock images.

  • Vanilla Concha

    The signature — a brioche-base concha made with French technique and a 24-hour ferment.

  • Chocolate Concha

    The same artisan concha under a chocolate shell — also in pistachio, mazapan and Nutella.

  • Pan de Muerto

    The traditional Day of the Dead sweet bread, sugar-dusted — regular and especial.

  • Tres Leches Slice

    Milk-soaked sponge with whipped cream — including a guava tres leches.

  • Cinnamon Roll

    Soft, swirled and iced — one of the most ordered items in listings.

  • Chocolatines

    Flaky chocolate croissants, baked fresh.

  • Cheesecake

    Cheesecake desserts topped with fresh fruit.

  • Cafe de Olla

    Traditional spiced coffee with cinnamon and piloncillo, served in a clay mug.

The concept

A full page, built around the favourites

This demo turns the items visitors name in public listings into a complete visit — menu, gallery, and directions in one place.

The menu above lists visitor-reported favourites, not a verified menu, and every photo on this page is illustrative stock — not photography of this business. What this concept adds is structure: the favourites up front, the visit details in one place, and a clear next step at the bottom.

Artesana is run by Tomas Valles and Luisa del Castillo, three years in at 1810 Trawood Drive — and now opening a second location in the renovated Kress Building downtown. Their conchas are made on a brioche base with a 24-hour ferment, alongside tres leches with guava, cheesecake and almond-flour cookies. If anything here looks out of date, the fastest check is a phone call.

Why this page works

Three things, done properly
